# agentgateway_traffic_routes (Data Source)

Lists the `traffic.route` config resources the gateway holds, sorted by id. Use `name_prefix` to narrow the listing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every route the agentgateway currently holds, sorted by id.
data "agentgateway_traffic_routes" "all" {}

# Narrow the listing to routes whose name starts with "api-".
data "agentgateway_traffic_routes" "api" {
  name_prefix = "api-"
}

output "route_hostnames" {
  value = {
    for route in data.agentgateway_traffic_routes.all.routes : route.name => route.hostnames
  }
}

# Backends are raw JSON objects; decode them to inspect a backend field. The
# list is sensitive because backend policies can carry credentials, so the
# output must be marked sensitive as well.
output "api_route_backends" {
  value = [
    for route in data.agentgateway_traffic_routes.api.routes : [
      for backend in route.backends : jsondecode(backend)
    ]
  ]
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name_prefix` (String) Only include routes whose name starts with this prefix. An empty prefix includes every route.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable identifier of the listing: `traffic.route:<name_prefix>`.
- `routes` (Attributes List) The matching routes, sorted by id. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes))

<a id="nestedatt--routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes`

Read-Only:

- `backends` (List of String, Sensitive) Backends of the route, each as its raw JSON object. Use `jsondecode` to inspect one.
- `gateways` (List of String) Gateways the route is attached to.
- `hostnames` (List of String) Hostnames the route matches.
- `name` (String) Route name, which is also the resource id.
